6.4. Command-Line Tools#

SUEWS (Surface Urban Energy and Water Balance Scheme) provides command-line tools for common operations without requiring Python scripting.

All tools are subcommands of a single suews command. Run suews --help for the list, and suews <subcommand> --help for the options of each one. Most subcommands accept --format json, which writes the standard SUEWS JSON envelope to stdout (see JSON Output Format).

Note

The hyphenated commands suews-run, suews-convert, suews-validate, suews-schema and suews-inspect are deprecated aliases of suews run, suews convert, suews validate, suews schema and suews inspect. They still work but print a DEPRECATED: notice to stderr and will be removed in a future release.

6.4.1. CLI Reference#

The command, argument, option and default listings below are generated directly from the suews Click definitions using sphinx_click.ext.

6.4.1.1. suews#

SUEWS unified command-line interface.

Use suews <subcommand> --help to see options for each subcommand. All subcommands emit a standard JSON envelope when invoked with --format json (where supported).

Usage

suews [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

6.4.1.1.1. compare#

Compare two SUEWS run directories, canonical Parquet outputs (monolithic files or streamed dataset directories), or a run and an observations CSV by computing per-variable RMSE / bias / Pearson r over the timestamps they share. Time-axis overlap and the grid used on each side are reported alongside; n counts finite paired samples.

Usage

suews compare [OPTIONS] RUN_A RUN_B_OR_OBS

Options

--metrics <metrics>#

Comma-separated metric names. Subset of {rmse,bias,r}.

Default:

'rmse,bias,r'

--variables <variables>#

Comma-separated variable names to compare.

Default:

'QH,QE,QN'

--grid <grid>#

Grid identity to compare when an input holds several grids (required in that case). Applied to both inputs.

--align <alignment>#

‘time’ aligns on shared timestamps and rejects inputs without a recoverable time axis; ‘positional’ compares rows by order and is labelled as such in the output.

Default:

'time'

Options:

time | positional

--format <output_format>#

Output format. ‘json’ emits the standard SUEWS envelope on stdout.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

Arguments

RUN_A#

Required argument

RUN_B_OR_OBS#

Required argument

6.4.1.1.2. contracts#

Inspect, export, publish, and validate versioned SUEWS forcing and output data contracts.

Usage

suews contracts [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
6.4.1.1.2.1. export#

Export a forcing or output contract artefact or release bundle.

Usage

suews contracts export [OPTIONS] {forcing|output}

Options

--version <contract_version>#

Contract version to export.

Default:

'current version'

--artefact <artefact>#

Artefact to export. Choices: catalogue, schema, manifest, bundle.

Default:

'catalogue'

Options:

catalogue | schema | manifest | bundle

-o, --output <output_path>#

Destination file path, or destination directory for bundle exports. Omit to write a single artefact to stdout.

--format <output_format>#

Status output format when writing to –output, or envelope mode on stdout. Choices: text, json.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

Arguments

INTERFACE#

Required argument

Default:

'https://suews.io'

--format <output_format>#

Output format. Choices: text, json.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

Arguments

INTERFACE#

Optional argument

6.4.1.1.3. convert#

Convert any supported SUEWS input into a current-schema YAML.

Input type is auto-detected from the file:

  • RunControl.nml / .nml: legacy SUEWS table set

  • .csv / .pkl: df_state snapshot

  • .yml / .yaml: older-release YAML (cross-release upgrade)

Pass -f/--from to disambiguate the source version when auto-detection is ambiguous (table releases for .nml inputs; release tag or schema version for .yml inputs).

Usage

suews convert [OPTIONS]

Options

-f, --from <fromVer>#

Source version. For .nml inputs pick a table release (e.g. 2024a); for .yml inputs pass a supy release tag (e.g. 2026.1.28) or a schema version. Auto-detected when omitted.

-i, --input <input_file>#

Input file: RunControl.nml for tables, .csv/.pkl for df_state, or .yml/.yaml for an older YAML config.

-o, --output <output_file>#

Output YAML file path

-d, --debug-dir <debug_dir>#

Optional directory to keep intermediate conversion files for debugging table/df_state runs. Ignored for YAML upgrades.

--no-profile-validation#

Disable automatic profile validation and creation of missing profiles (table/df_state paths only).

--format <output_format>#

Output format. ‘json’ emits the standard SUEWS envelope on stdout.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

--forcing <forcing>#

Legacy forcing table for coordinated soil conversion.

--forcing-output <forcing_output>#

New canonical forcing table.

--manifest <manifest>#

New JSON conversion manifest.

--source-contract <source_contract>#

Forcing contract of a positional (headerless) forcing file; 1.0.0-1.2.0 carry legacy xsmd, 2.0.0 carries sm.

Options:

1.0.0 | 1.1.0 | 1.2.0 | 2.0.0

--source-unit <source_unit>#

Confirmed unit of the forcing soil column. Legacy xsmd with the ambiguous ‘observed’ selector: ‘m3 m-3’ (volumetric) or ‘kg kg-1’ (gravimetric). Legacy xsmd with modelled soil moisture: ‘m3 m-3’, ‘kg kg-1’ or ‘mm’. Canonical sm: ‘kg m-2’ only.

Options:

m3 m-3 | kg kg-1 | mm | kg m-2

--layer-top <layer_top>#

Confirmed represented layer top in m (explicit 0 for the whole store).

--layer-depth <layer_depth>#

Confirmed represented layer thickness in m.

--legacy-depth-is-thickness#

Confirm old depth describes layer thickness.

--drop-legacy#

Archive and drop unused method-0 xsmd values with a recorded reason.

--dry-run#

Report conversion and missing decisions without writing files.

6.4.1.1.4. diagnose#

Read a SUEWS run directory (or a canonical output file / streamed Parquet dataset directory) and run a battery of Phase-1 checks (provenance present, output files present, NaN proportion in QH/QE/QN, energy-balance closure). When given a run directory, writes a diagnostics.json sidecar inside it; when given a direct output file or streamed Parquet dataset directory, resolves provenance.json beside the target and intentionally omits diagnostics.json to keep the Parquet dataset clean and avoid overwriting a sibling or enclosing run sidecar. Use –format json for structured output consumable by MCP tooling.

Usage

suews diagnose [OPTIONS] RUN_DIR

Options

--format <output_format>#

Output format. ‘json’ emits the standard SUEWS envelope on stdout.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

Arguments

RUN_DIR#

Required argument

6.4.1.1.5. init#

Initialise a new SUEWS case directory by copying a packaged template into TARGET_DIR. The directory is created if missing; existing config files are not overwritten. Currently only the ‘simple-urban’ template is shipped; the other names are reserved and rejected with a structured error envelope.

Usage

suews init [OPTIONS] TARGET_DIR

Options

--template <template>#

Template to scaffold from.

Default:

'simple-urban'

Options:

multi-site | simple-urban | spartacus | teaching-demo

--format <output_format>#

Output format. ‘json’ emits the standard SUEWS envelope on stdout.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

Arguments

TARGET_DIR#

Required argument

6.4.1.1.6. inspect#

Show a compact overview of a SUEWS YAML config: per-site coordinates, surface-cover fractions, forcing file summary. Read-only — never modifies the config. Use –format json for structured output.

Usage

suews inspect [OPTIONS] CONFIG_PATH

Options

--format <output_format>#

Output format. ‘json’ emits the standard SUEWS envelope on stdout.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

Arguments

CONFIG_PATH#

Required argument

6.4.1.1.8. run#

Run SUEWS simulation using YAML (recommended) or namelist configuration.

YAML Configuration (Recommended):

$ suews run config.yml
$ suews run /path/to/config.yml

Set model.control.output.dir to choose where results are written. If the output block is absent, source YAML can use the legacy model.control.output_file.path. If the selected directory is missing, null or an empty string, results go to the directory where you invoke this command. A non-empty relative path starts from the source YAML file’s directory. Use . to write beside that file.

Namelist Configuration (Deprecated):

$ suews run -p RunControl.nml
$ suews run -p /path/to/RunControl.nml

The format is auto-detected based on file extension:

  • .yml, .yaml: YAML format (modern, recommended)

  • .nml: Namelist format (legacy, deprecated)

To migrate from namelist to YAML:

$ suews convert -i RunControl.nml -o config.yml
$ suews run config.yml

For more information, see: https://docs.suews.io/

Usage

suews run [OPTIONS] [CONFIG_FILE]

Options

-p, --path_runcontrol <path_runcontrol>#

[DEPRECATED] Path to RunControl namelist file. Use positional argument instead.

Arguments

CONFIG_FILE#

Optional argument

6.4.1.1.9. schema#

SUEWS Schema Management - Manage YAML configuration schemas.

This tool provides utilities for managing SUEWS YAML configuration schemas, including version checking, migration between versions, and schema export.

When invoked without a subcommand (suews schema [--version V] [--format json|text]), it returns a single envelope wrapping the JSON Schema for the requested (or current) version.

Usage

suews schema [OPTIONS] [COMMAND] [ARGS]...

Options

-v, --verbose#

Enable verbose output

-q, --quiet#

Suppress non-essential output

--version <schema_version>#

Schema version to expose. Defaults to the current schema version. Only consulted when no subcommand is given.

--format <out_format>#

Output format when suews schema is called without a subcommand. ‘json’ emits the canonical SUEWS envelope on stdout.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

6.4.1.1.9.1. convert-soil#

Convert any supported SUEWS input into a current-schema YAML.

Input type is auto-detected from the file:

  • RunControl.nml / .nml: legacy SUEWS table set

  • .csv / .pkl: df_state snapshot

  • .yml / .yaml: older-release YAML (cross-release upgrade)

Pass -f/--from to disambiguate the source version when auto-detection is ambiguous (table releases for .nml inputs; release tag or schema version for .yml inputs).

Usage

suews schema convert-soil [OPTIONS]

Options

-f, --from <fromVer>#

Source version. For .nml inputs pick a table release (e.g. 2024a); for .yml inputs pass a supy release tag (e.g. 2026.1.28) or a schema version. Auto-detected when omitted.

-i, --input <input_file>#

Input file: RunControl.nml for tables, .csv/.pkl for df_state, or .yml/.yaml for an older YAML config.

-o, --output <output_file>#

Output YAML file path

-d, --debug-dir <debug_dir>#

Optional directory to keep intermediate conversion files for debugging table/df_state runs. Ignored for YAML upgrades.

--no-profile-validation#

Disable automatic profile validation and creation of missing profiles (table/df_state paths only).

--format <output_format>#

Output format. ‘json’ emits the standard SUEWS envelope on stdout.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

--forcing <forcing>#

Legacy forcing table for coordinated soil conversion.

--forcing-output <forcing_output>#

New canonical forcing table.

--manifest <manifest>#

New JSON conversion manifest.

--source-contract <source_contract>#

Forcing contract of a positional (headerless) forcing file; 1.0.0-1.2.0 carry legacy xsmd, 2.0.0 carries sm.

Options:

1.0.0 | 1.1.0 | 1.2.0 | 2.0.0

--source-unit <source_unit>#

Confirmed unit of the forcing soil column. Legacy xsmd with the ambiguous ‘observed’ selector: ‘m3 m-3’ (volumetric) or ‘kg kg-1’ (gravimetric). Legacy xsmd with modelled soil moisture: ‘m3 m-3’, ‘kg kg-1’ or ‘mm’. Canonical sm: ‘kg m-2’ only.

Options:

m3 m-3 | kg kg-1 | mm | kg m-2

--layer-top <layer_top>#

Confirmed represented layer top in m (explicit 0 for the whole store).

--layer-depth <layer_depth>#

Confirmed represented layer thickness in m.

--legacy-depth-is-thickness#

Confirm old depth describes layer thickness.

--drop-legacy#

Archive and drop unused method-0 xsmd values with a recorded reason.

--dry-run#

Report conversion and missing decisions without writing files.

6.4.1.1.9.2. export#

Export the JSON Schema for SUEWS configurations.

Examples:

suews schema export -o schema.json
suews schema export --version 1.0 --format yaml

Usage

suews schema export [OPTIONS]

Options

-o, --output <output>#

Output file for schema

--version <version>#

Schema version to export

--format <format>#

Output format

Default:

'json'

Options:

json | yaml

6.4.1.1.9.3. info#

Display information about available schema versions.

Usage

suews schema info [OPTIONS]
6.4.1.1.9.4. migrate#

Migrate configuration files between schema versions.

The input files are left unchanged; migrated copies are written next to them as <name>.migrated.yml, or into –output-dir. For schema 2026.6.dev16, replace invalid vegetation sdd_id values with finite site or restart data. An omitted field initialises that vegetation type at zero.

Examples:

suews schema migrate old_config.yml
suews schema migrate configs/*.yml --output-dir migrated/

Usage

suews schema migrate [OPTIONS] FILES...

Options

--target-version <target_version>#

Target schema version for migration (omit to migrate to the current installed schema)

-o, --output-dir <output_dir>#

Output directory for migrated files

-n, --dry-run#

Show what would be done without doing it

Arguments

FILES#

Required argument(s)

6.4.1.1.9.5. version#

Check or update schema versions in configuration files.

Examples:

suews schema version config.yml
suews schema version *.yml --update --target-version 1.0

Usage

suews schema version [OPTIONS] FILES...

Options

-u, --update#

Update schema version in files

--target-version <target_version>#

Target version for update

-b, --backup, --no-backup#

Keep a timestamped copy of each file before updating it

Default:

True

Arguments

FILES#

Required argument(s)

6.4.1.1.10. summarise#

Print a per-variable summary (mean / min / max / NaN-percentage) of a SUEWS run directory, streamed Parquet dataset directory or standalone output file. Multi-group Parquet outputs preserve each (group, variable) series independently. Pass –variables to restrict the columns using bare names (e.g. QH,QE,QN) or group-qualified names (e.g. SUEWS.QS,ESTM.QS); the default is every numeric column.

Examples:

suews summarise path/to/run_dir
suews summarise path/to/run_dir –variables QH,QE,QN
suews summarise path/to/run_dir –variables SUEWS.QS,ESTM.QS

Usage

suews summarise [OPTIONS] RUN_DIR

Options

--variables <variables>#

Comma-separated variable names (e.g. QH,QE,QN) or group-qualified names (e.g. SUEWS.QS,ESTM.QS). A bare name that appears in multiple groups summarises all matching groups with a note.

Default:

'every numeric column'

--format <output_format>#

Output format. ‘json’ emits the standard SUEWS envelope on stdout.

Default:

'text'

Options:

text | json

Arguments

RUN_DIR#

Required argument

SUEWS Configuration Validator.

Default behaviour: run the complete validation pipeline on one FILE. Use -p C --dry-run FILES... for read-only schema checks on one or more files; use suews schema for schema lifecycle operations.

Phase pipeline to run

'ABC'

A | B | C | AB | AC | BC | ABC

Validation mode for phase pipeline

Default:

'public'

public | dev

--dry-run#

Do not write files; validate only (supports pipeline C and ABC)

--format <out_format>#

Output format for --dry-run results

'table'

table | json

--schema-version <schema_version>#

Schema version to validate against in --dry-run

-f, --forcing <forcing>#

Enable/disable forcing data validation

Default:

'on'

Options:

on | off

--science-fixes <science_fixes>#

Handle Phase B scientific transformations: suggest, apply, or off

Default:

'suggest'

Options:

suggest | apply | off

--continue-on-error#

Continue running downstream read-only phases after an earlier phase reports errors

FILES#

6.4.2. YAML Validation and Engine Contract for suews run#

suews run does not hand your YAML file to the physics engine as written. It first loads it through the SUEWS data model, the same path as SUEWSSimulation: the configuration is validated, any parameter you leave out takes its documented data-model default, and the result is passed to the engine as a complete, resolved configuration. Errors in the YAML are therefore reported by the data model, naming the field concerned, before any simulation starts.

Set model.control.output.dir in source YAML to choose where suews run writes results. The command uses the legacy model.control.output_file.path only when the model.control.output block is absent. If the selected directory is missing, null or an empty string, the command writes to the directory where you invoked it. A non-empty relative path starts from the source YAML file’s directory. Use . to write beside the source file.

Resolved input is the caller contract: defaults belong in the data model, and callers must pass the engine a complete, resolved configuration. Enforcement of this contract at the engine boundary is still being completed; some omitted values can still retain legacy bridge fallbacks. Acceptance by the engine does not establish that an incomplete configuration is valid.

The resolved model.control.forcing.timestamp_reference must explicitly contain local_standard_time or utc (a bare string or a value wrapper). The engine rejects missing, null, malformed and unknown values with the full field path. The source configuration still defaults to local_standard_time through the data model. The values follow and daylight apply only to model.control.output.timestamp_reference, which labels saved output.

The resolved model.physics.storage_heat must also be present as a valid storage-heat selector (integer code, accepted scheme name, family form or supported legacy alias, bare or in a value wrapper). Missing, null, non-finite, fractional, out-of-range-integer or wrong-type values are rejected with the field path model.physics.storage_heat instead of silently falling back to 0 (observed storage heat). Source configurations still default to 1 (ohm / OHM_WITHOUT_QF) through the data model.

Resolved physics input also requires explicit values for the four aerodynamic selectors model.physics.roughness_length_momentum, model.physics.roughness_length_heat, model.physics.roughness_sublayer and model.physics.roughness_sublayer_level (an integer, value wrapper or registered readable name). All four values are required, including roughness_sublayer_level under MOST (roughness_sublayer=0). For missing, null, non-finite or malformed numeric values, the error identifies the full field path. For an unrecognised scheme name, the error identifies the selector and the name supplied. Source YAML continues to receive the data model defaults (2/variable, 2/kawai, 2/variable and 0/none).

If you kept a resolved file from an earlier release, run the original source configuration with suews run source.yml. To save a new resolved file for suews-engine, use the current SuPy installation and keep the new file beside the source so supplied relative paths still resolve correctly:

from pathlib import Path
from supy.data_model import SUEWSConfig
from supy._run_rust import config_to_engine_yaml

source = Path("source.yml")
config = SUEWSConfig.from_yaml(source)
source.with_name("resolved.yml").write_text(config_to_engine_yaml(config), encoding="utf-8")

Note

The SuPy package also contains a suews-engine binary, the Rust runtime that suews run drives. It is a developer and test tool, not a user command: suews-engine run expects a configuration that has already been resolved in this way, and does not perform data-model validation or resolution for a hand-written YAML file. To run a configuration, use suews run.

File execution requires a string at model.control.output.dir (a value wrapper is also accepted). Export with config_to_engine_yaml from supy._run_rust. If the selected source directory is missing or null, the export records the absolute working directory of the process that calls config_to_engine_yaml. The engine writes there even when launched from another directory.

With an explicit empty string (dir: ""), the engine writes beside the exported YAML. A relative path, including ., also starts from the exported file’s directory. Keep the export beside its source to preserve that base. An absolute path keeps its original destination.

A standalone file containing only the legacy model.control.output_file.path is rejected. Move its value to model.control.output.dir before running the file.

Ordinary model dumps and to_yaml() remain portable source exports and leave an omitted directory unset. Buffer-only library calls return arrays and leave an omitted directory unset, including when the current working directory is unavailable. The public Python save(path) argument still takes precedence over the configured directory.

Each resolved site must supply all four LUMPS parameters in sites[].properties.lumps, including raincover, rainmaxres, drainrt and veg_type. When an ordinary source configuration omits the block or a field, SuPy supplies the documented defaults during export. Regenerate an incomplete engine input from its source configuration.
